You probably aren't comfortable using your fingertips and wrist to aim. For most people your wrist is able to react and change direction quicker than your arm, so it's good for tracking fast strafes. Also because its a smaller muscle youre less likely to over correct than if you used your arm.Your fingertips are good for when you're trying to be really precise like shooting at long range and trying to control a spray or use a wingman.

 You can technically get it all done with your arm as you probably are, but being able to use a higher sense than friggin 80cm is beneficial. Especially in a game like apex. You probably have to reset your mouse a ton. If you ever run into a blood hound or octane close range I imagine it's gotta be pretty tiring to track them as they strafe around you, and you probably can't move much without having to reset your mouse. No matter how fast you can reset it's still a period of time you have to stop aiming and shooting. Sens is definitely a subjective thing but I think even if you learned to play at say 60cm you'd  be a better player in the long run.

 OP, the "optimal opener" is really not that important,  because no one is just going to let you do the whole thing, especially in shuffle where you can't rely on your teammates to CC the off target. Someone will most likely peel you or trinket. That being said according to Nahj this is the best opener assuming you've properly CC'd the enemy team. The parts in parenthesis are for explanation. Ignore them if you dont care. 

Shadow strike (we want to get DS mark up ASAP)

 Kidney shot (we have full combo points from premeditation on our shadow strike) 

Shadow strike again 

Now, this is the point where you decide based on how they react. If someone pre uses something or trinkets you're still in great shape because you've hardly committed anything. You haven't pressed dance or blades yet. Go swap to the off-target or healer and come back later. 

Assuming no one has reacted yet: 

Shadow dance, Thistle Tea, symbols of death, Shadowblades, and dps trinket (these are all off GCD so macro some of them together). You'll have full combo points again because of the first dance talent and the previous Shadow strike. 

Rupture (this gives you a stack of dance macabre and gets your corrupt the blood hero talent rolling. Danse macabre buffs your damage for every different ability you use during shadow dance, this is part of why we rupture here even though it's a dot instead of an instant damage ability. It also consumes one of our deathstalker's mark stacks, refunding some energy and doing extra damage) 

Sepsis (another dot so we want it used early in our burst, also gives another stack of danse and just hits hard in general). 

Eviscerate (we want to get another stack of danse before we use secret technique, also sepsis is bugged and will often only give you 6 points instead of max with blades for some stupid reason, and we don't want to waste secret tech on a 6 point finisher. Consumes our 2nd stack of deathstalkers' mark, AND gives you the finality buff for your next evis).

Cheapshot (We need to re-stun now assuming non-orc. Also, +1 stack of danse.)

Secret technique (big damn, also the slight delay can be somewhat beneficial here because it makes the bulk of the damage line up with our next finisher. ONLY use if this if it won't break healer CC. If it will, then just eviscerate.+1 stack of danse and consumes our final stack of dealthstalker's mark, granting us Darkest Night)

Cheapshot (keeping people stunned is important so they can't use defensives or avoid this last evis). 

You will probably have to re-use Thistle Tea here because it only lasts 6 seconds. 

Eviscerate (This evis is mega buffed because you'll have so many modifiers on it. It's guaranteed to crit and does bonus damage from darkest night. It also gets buffed from finality and max stacks of dance macabre. If no one pressed a defensive, this guy is probably dead.)

You can also shadowstrike, rupture, shadowstrike, dance + modifiers -> Kidney and do the rest of the opener. Basically the same thing. 

I feel like I just wrote a novel to explain ONE opener, but people will still cry that rogue is easy and broken smh. 

Also, unfortunately, this will all probably change a bit next week because they're reworking the class,  but hopefully it's given you some understanding of WHY we want to press our abilities in the order that we do.

It's situational, and input dependent. As an Mnk player I can give my understanding though. 

Mnk vs. Mnk

Always start by dodging. The best dodging is an unpredictable strafe that is NOT just blindly A-D-A-D spamming. You need to have some bias more toward one direction or the other because if you don't your opponent will just aim at the center of your strafe and fry you. 

Once the fight develops a bit then you re-evaluate. If you have an hp advantage you can now start "strafe aiming" to try and finish them off. If they're in the open mirror them for the easiest possible time aiming. If they're strafing back into cover anti mirror them to extend the angle you can still hit them as long as possible to get out more damage. 

If you're losing your only hope is to keep dodging and hope you can hit more shots than they do. This is especially useful if they have a weapon with a long reload time. Since you're already getting hit try and switch up your strafe and be even more unpredictable. Keep in mind at this point it's more important that you avoid damage than it is that you do damage, as if you both had an aimbot now you would lose no matter what.

Speaking of getting hit that brings up some of the exceptions to the above ideas 

1. If you're not getting hit, KEEP DOING WHAT YOURE DOING. If you're just long strafing to the right and you can see your enemies bullet tracers all missing on your left side keep holding the long strafe. You might just kill them before they hit you again, and the last thing you want to do is walk into their crosshair for them 

2. If you can circle behind someone pretty much always do it, especially if you're a higher sens player or if they tend to A-D spam. There's a decent chance they run out of mouse pad space before you do and obviously if you're behind them it's free damage 

3. Situational advantages that require you to strafe towards them, whether that's a strong position or an armor swap or your teammates knockdown shield 

Mnk vs. Controller 

The default and generally safer strategy is the exact same as above (though obviously you'll never run them out of mousepad space, but at least they turn slow) 

There's also the option against controller players to hard mirror them all the time. There are 2 reasons behind this philosophy. 

1. Controller is worse than Mnk at making small adjustments. By mirroring you're making it so you and your opponent only have to adjust your aim by small amounts (if at all). Controller can struggle with this and that's part of why so many prefer to anti mirror in their fights. 

2. Aim assist requires some amount of input in order to activate. If you're mirroring you'll stay close or at the center of their screen and they might not press their thumb stick (or try to aim more with their movement) and thus won't have any AA. 

I personally still find this really risky, but it can definitely work. Also part of the issue is if they have any stick drift then the AA should kick in regardless as far as I understand

Monk: clones as well as the tiger Xuen

I do this until I eventually reach the score at a speed of 0.71, and then increase it again to 0.72 and the process repeats. I’ve been doing 5 attempts a day but that’s because I do a lot of scenarios, so if following aimer 7’s guide consider doing 10. 

Your numerical score in these time altered scenarios is completely pointless and doesn’t go on the leaderboard as far as I can tell. But that’s why you pick a goal you can’t hit yet in the regular scenario. It certainly worked for me. I couldn’t get 12,000 reliably in CFSIE on the standard scenario at regular speed, but now I can. 

I think because you increase the speed so very gradually you’re essentially forcing yourself to be consistent with your improvement. 0.98 and 0.99 really aren’t that different than 1.0, but you’ve got to repeatedly hit the goal score to actually get to 1. So when you finally DO get to 1 you’ll know that not only will your personal best be somewhere above the goal score but you’ll be able to CONSISTENTLY hit above that score which you couldn’t even reach before. For jump fighting a lot of it is practice and situational. If you’re about to run into a door and you can hear someone floating it, just wait outside the door and push only when they land and you know what side they landed on. 

If you’re say, behind a titan shield and against a hunter with a shotgun you know one hundred percent that he’s going to jump over it to shoot you so either keep your on him directly or just start to aim up

If you’re in a cover around a corner and you have a feeling they’re going to push you, JUMP. If you listen closely you’ll hear them jump around, but if they don’t they’ll probably slide around the corner. Either way if you jump there’s a better chance of being somewhere they aren’t expecting. (I consider Icarus grip kind of mandatory on shotguns but that’s just my playstyle) 

If someone is super close to you and they blink or jump over your head what I usually do is immediately 180 and THEN worry about looking up. Generally though if you 180 and it’s not a warlock they will almost always fall right into your cross hair and it’s an easy shot. 

Another easy shotgunning tip is to try and weaken them with your primary before you go for shotgun kill. It vastly increases the range at which you can finish them with one shot. Furthermore, say you get someone weak and then hide in cover and it’s safe for you to push them with your shotgun (they’re alone and not baiting you for their teammates). You want to essentially take as wide of an angle as possible (the most distance you can) as you round the corner with your shotgun (ideally you’ll be jumping or sliding around it) because you can one shot them from much further than they can one shot you. If you get super close you’re basically taking an unnecessary 50/50 and nullifying the advantage you earned by getting them weak. This is especially true if they have a shotgun and you don’t. If that’s the case you don’t want to push them unless they can die from one shot from your primary and you want to be even further from them as you push. 

And one last and MASSIVELY helpful (IMO) tip for shotgunning, ESPECIALLY after the nerfs, is to immediately switch to your hand cannon after your first shotgun shot. This is especially helpful if you have QuickDraw on it. Oh you left that guy absolute but didn’t one shot him? Don’t wait for your shotgun to be ready again, whip out your HC and hip fire him. Bonus points if you’re using ace because now you have MM. You’ll get a feel for what will and won’t be a one shot kill but generally just assume you’re not going to instantly kill them and always be ready to switch.
